title: signal-orchestra-rollout-conductor-playbook-wip
body:
Purpose: This is a working playbook describing an orchestration-first approach to cross-functional rollouts (we call it the Signal Orchestra). The goal is to give a single runbook that teams can use to coordinate canaries, A/B slices, and progressive exposure for LLM-backed features while preserving fast rollback and clear owner responsibilities.

Scope: Applies to staged feature launches across hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment surfaces where customer-visible model or routing changes are introduced. Not for infra-only, backend-only data migrations unless they change inference surface behavior.

Key metaphors and glossary (quick):
- Signal Orchestra: the set of telemetry signals we monitor in lockstep during an exposure.
- Conductor: the person who coordinates the rollout cadence and comms.
- Section Leads: owners for groups of signals (latency, cost, quality, infra errors, safety).
- Safety Curtain: pre-configured abort policy and fast-fail path.
- Rehearsal / Dress Rehearsal Canary: a synthetic traffic run to exercise observability and fallback before user exposure.

Stakeholders and roles (cross-functional choreography):
- Product (Conductor): sets hypothesis, acceptance criteria, and lead comms.
- Eng Release Owner (Runbook executor): triggers exposures, config flips, and monitors infra signals.
- SRE / Platform (Section Lead - Infra): watches capacity, OOMs, queuing, and routing correctness.
- Applied ML / Research (Section Lead - Quality): watches semantic quality metrics, hallucination signals, rerank drift, and eval set regressions.
- Data & Observability (Section Lead - Telemetry): ensures dashboards, alerting, and instrumentation are green.
- Trust & Safety / Compliance (Section Lead - Safety): watches safety classifier hits, escalation filters, and audit logs.
- CS / Support: prepped comms and escalation path if customer-visible regressions appear.

Experiment taxonomy and when to use each pattern:
1) Micro-Canary (0.1% -> 1%): low-risk config change, model patch, or routing variant. Use when latency/cost behavior is the primary unknown.
2) Behavior Canary (1% -> 5%): for model behavior changes where semantic drift or user-facing outputs matter. Includes small-sample human review.
3) A/B Cohort (50/50 or weighted): feature-level comparison for product impact. Needs pre-registered metric set and sample-size plan.
4) Hybrid Staged (multi-wave): combine canaries + A/B for large rollouts where risk is orthogonal across signals.

Signal Orchestra (primary signals to monitor in parallel):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (model and user-perceived)
- Token cost per request / tokens per session
- Error rate: 500s, client-timeouts, model-timeouts
- Queueing depth / backpressure metrics
- Model quality signals: automated eval score, rerank delta, embedding-sim drift
- Safety hits: classifier rate, escalation count, denial-of-service filters
- Customer impact indicators: CS tickets, NPS message deltas, account-level anomalies

Safety Curtain (abort rules and priority):
- Immediate aborts: sustained p99 latency > baseline * 3 for > 5 minutes, infra OOMs on serving hosts, fatal panics or mismatch in routing table, safety classifier spike > x10 baseline for 5 minutes.
- Soft abort / throttle: token-cost > baseline * 2 for > 30 minutes, increased tail-latency without errors, quality score drop > 10% on agreed eval set.
- Graceful rollback plan: switch routing to previous variant, switch to cached responses for high-frequency flows, scale up fallback model pool. Test rollback script in staging weekly.

Telemetry and dashboards (must haves before exposure):
- Single pane view (Signal Orchestra dashboard) showing the above signals with anchors for baseline and current cohort.
- Drift snapshots: side-by-side token-level distributions and semantic eval snapshots.
- Cohort tracer: request-sampling that surfaces full prompt + model output + routing path for failing requests.
- Canary heartbeat synthetic traffic: run synthetic cohort every 5 minutes and graph health.

Canary cadence and timing recommendations:
- Rehearsal (internal synthetic): 1–2 days before any external exposure. Verify rollback and alerting.
- Micro-Canary window: 1–3 hours at 0.1% then pause for signal review; expand in doubling increments after each verified window.
- Behavior Canary window: hold minimum 24 hours at each exposure step to capture business-hour behavior and overnight batch effects.
- A/B studies: plan durations based on statistical power; default to 14 days for user-facing KPIs unless power calc indicates otherwise.

Checklists (pre-launch):
- [ ] Conductor confirmed hypothesis and accepted metrics, written in the rollout ticket.
- [ ] Owners assigned for each Section Lead with contact phone-on-call.
- [ ] Signal Orchestra dashboard deployed and validated.
- [ ] Linked smoke tests and rehearsal synthetic run executed.
- [ ] Rollback playbook validated in staging and accessible.
- [ ] Customer comms drafted and CS briefed.
- [ ] Escalation tree and oncall rota published for the rollout window.

Checklist (go/no-go criteria at each step):
- Green: all Section Leads report no anomalies, synthetic runs stable, no safety escalations.
- Amber: one medium-level metric breach (e.g., token-cost or p95 latency) — hold expansion, run targeted mitigations.
- Red: abort and rollback. Document incident and follow up with postmortem.

Communication plan template (short):
- Pre-launch: Slack thread + weekly sync with Conductor and Section Leads.
- During rollout: pinned rollout thread with minute-by-minute updates during micro-canary windows, hourly updates during behavior canaries.
- Post-launch: summary of signals, decision rationale, and action items in rollout ticket and confluence.

Data retention and privacy notes: for Private/Dedicated customers, ensure sampling and cohort tracing comply with tenant data policies; default to PII redaction and only sample aggregated deltas for those customers unless explicit consent or audit path exists.

Open questions / discussion points (working):
- What are the authoritative thresholds for safety-classifier spikes? (T&S to propose SIGMA and absolute rates)
- How should we automate the decision threshold between soft-abort and hard-abort? (SRE + Product to prototype)
- Can we add canned rollback runbooks to the console to make switchovers one-click? (Product + Eng)

Appendix: quick templates
- Rollout ticket template: hypothesis, primary metric, baseline numbers, exposure schedule, owners, rollback steps, linked dashboards, rehearsal evidence.
- Postmortem headline template: sequence of events, timeline, root cause, remediation, follow-ups.

Notes to self / collaboration log:
- 2024-11-05 Maya: initial draft with Signal Orchestra framing.
- 2024-11-08 Ravi: added rehearsal cadence and abort examples.
- 2024-11-12 Ana: telemetry checklist + synthetic heartbeat pattern.
- 2024-11-17 Liam: clarified hybrid staged pattern and communication template.

Next steps (action items):
- T&S: propose safety thresholds and add to this doc (due 2024-11-22).
- Platform: prototype one-click rollback in staging (POC by 2024-12-06).
- Data & Observability: bake Signal Orchestra dashboard into default rollout template (ETA 2024-12-01).

This is a working document — leave comments inline and add your name to the collaborators list if you want edit access. The goal is to iterate until this becomes the canonical cross-functional conductor playbook for staged LLM changes across our deployment surfaces.
